title: CSS Debugging Questions
definition: Scenario-based questions where you are presented with a broken layout and asked how you would diagnose and fix it.
simpleExplanation: The interviewer describes a bug: 'The horizontal scrollbar keeps appearing on mobile, but there are no elements wider than 100%. Why?'. You have to explain your thought process and Chrome DevTools workflow.
realWorldExample: Debugging margin collapse, z-index stacking context traps, or missing `box-sizing: border-box` resets.

basic: What is the easiest way to visually find an element that is causing a horizontal scrollbar??

answers.question: Find overflow elements?
answers.answer: Add `* { outline: 1px solid red; }` to your CSS. This instantly draws a red box around every single element on the page, revealing which one is sticking out past the screen edge.

answers.question: Margin Collapse?
answers.answer: If a top div has `margin-bottom: 30px` and the bottom div has `margin-top: 20px`, they don't add up to 50px! Vertical margins collapse into each other, and the browser just picks the largest one. So the total space between them will be exactly 30px.

Fixes: Margin collapse only happens in normal block flow. If you change the parent to a Flexbox container (`display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 80px;`), margin collapse is completely disabled!
